articles.title: Marvel’s Wolverine Limited-Edition PS5 Controller Is Still Available for Preorder (But It May Sell Out)
articles.summary: The big PS5 exclusive this fall is Marvel’s Wolverine. It’s Insomniac Studios’ follow-up to the excellent (and massively successful) Spider-Man games, and it promises to be a bloody good time.
body: Functionally, Marvel’s Wolverine Limited-Edition PS5 DualSense Wireless Controller is a standard PS5 controller. What makes it stand out is the design, which makes it look like Wolverine got mad while playing Fortnite and attacked the thing. It features three jagged claw marks across the face of the controller. The marks are vibrant yellow, set against the black of the grips and touchpad. It looks fierce.

The bottom of the controller is also yellow, as are the shapes on the face buttons and the tiny arrows on the D-pad. On the left and right grips you’ll also find gray scuff marks that add to the battle-damage effect. Overall, it’s one of the coolest PS5 controller designs yet — and there have been a lot.

The controller actually comes in two variations. There’s a “Battle Yellow” one that’s bright and bold. Then there’s an “Adamantium” white one that features the same scuffed-and-clawed design, but with metallic white to accent the black, making it somewhat less flashy. The Adamantium white one was a PlayStation Direct exclusive, and it has, unfortunately, sold out.
points: The big PS5 exclusive this fall is Marvel’s Wolverine.
It’s Insomniac Studios’ follow-up to the excellent (and massively successful) Spider-Man games, and it promises to be a bloody good time.

articles.title: The 10 Greatest Soulslikes of the Past 10 years, Ranked
articles.summary: With Elden Ring ’s arrival on Nintendo Switch 2 and FromSoftware’s The Duskbloods right around the corner, now’s as good of a time as any to reflect on the genre of games FromSoftware helped build by looking at the 10 best Soulslikes of the past 10 years.
body: Ever since the one-two punch of FromSoftware’s Demon’s Souls in 2009 and Dark Souls in 2011, the Soulslike genre has gradually grown in popularity. Recent years have given parry aficionados plenty of drab environments, grotesque enemies, and opaque stories to enjoy. Of course, not every Soulslike is filled with darkness; drenching its world in sun is what made 2024’s Enotria: The Last Song stand out, for example.

Of course, defining what exactly is a “Soulslike” can be a tricky endeavor, especially when so many recent games combine elements from various genres. We’re looking for games that are high on difficulty, encourage exploration, have bonfire-like checkpoints, and usually punish the player for dying. We’re limiting the list to one game per series, and excluding FromSoftware’s Soulsborne output. You already know Elden Ring is the best this genre has to offer this side of Bloodborne (the true GOAT).
points: With Elden Ring ’s arrival on Nintendo Switch 2 and FromSoftware’s The Duskbloods right around the corner, now’s as good of a time as any to reflect on the genre of games FromSoftware helped build by…

articles.title: 'One Piece Card Game' Is Collaborating With 'Final Fantasy's Best Artist
articles.summary: While it's not getting a full-on Final Fantasy collaboration like Magic: The Gathering, One Piece Card Game is doing the next best thing. This November, a booster pack will hit store shelves containing art by Yoshitaka Amano, one of the Final Fantasy series' most prolific artists.
body: At One Piece Day '26 this weekend, the highest-profile announcements were for things like new One Piece movies or the new cast members for the third season of the live-action show. One Piece Card Game also got a lot of new announcements at the event, including several previews of cards that will be part of Booster Pack Vol. 18 that comes out in Nov. 2026. While Franky, Nico Robin, and more are getting some great-looking new cards, the highlights of the booster pack are new Loki and Shamrock ones drawn by Yoshitaka Amano.

Amano has a storied history across anime and video games, most famously contributing to the Final Fantasy series in its earlier years. A lot of the iconic artwork and character designs that we associate with the first six Final Fantasy titles were created by Amano, and he still works with Square Enix to design the logos for new Final Fantasy games. In 2025, he contributed some new artwork for that franchise's crossover cards in Magic: The Gathering.
points: While it's not getting a full-on Final Fantasy collaboration like Magic: The Gathering, One Piece Card Game is doing the next best thing.

articles.title: Miyazaki explains how The Duskbloods plans to protect newcomers from its best players
articles.summary: FromSoftware is stepping into one of multiplayer gaming's most divisive arguments with The Duskbloods, confirming the upcoming Switch 2 exclusive will lean on skill-based matchmaking to keep newcomers safe from its most battle-hardened players.
body: Speaking to IGN, FromSoftware president and Duskbloods director Hidetaka Miyazaki confirmed the game will run on a ranked system, pairing highly skilled players together and keeping newer players in their own pool specifically to avoid lopsided matches as the game's skill gap widens over time.

Skill-based matchmaking has been a persistent flashpoint in multiplayer games for years. Games like Call of Duty and Apex Legends have repeatedly faced backlash from players who feel it makes lobbies feel unnecessarily punishing.

"In terms of really, really good players, we definitely plan on having the matchmaking system work in a way so that it's ranked, and players who are really good tend to be matched with other players who are great, and players who are new tend to be matched with other new players just to avoid situations like you had mentioned," he explained.

articles.title: 'It Ends' Director Alex Ullom Reveals the Movie's Meaning and His Surprising Sequel Plan
articles.summary: This was 2020, during COVID quarantine, and Ullom was spending a lot of time playing online poker in a virtual reality Oculus app. He wasn't just killing time, though. He was looking for investors.
body: Six years ago, Alex Ullom wasn't the young director behind one of 2026's buzziest horror movies. He was just a recent film school graduate with a trippy script about four kids like him who drive off from college to start their new lives — and instead wind up stuck on an endless road that defies the laws of space and time.

"I would just sit in virtual reality anonymous poker lobbies online for hours on end and hang out with people and shoot the shit," Ullom tells Polygon via a Zoom call from his apartment. "A small part of me was like, I definitely could meet an investor."

Ullom filmed the first version of It Ends in 2022, then brought a rough cut to some early investors and asked for the cash to reshoot most of the movie. It Ends premiered at SXSW in 2025 and released digitally on the Letterboxd Video Store that December. Then, it was picked up by Neon, which saw potential for the movie to be the latest installment in a recent string of industry-defying low-budget, high-profit horror flicks. It Ends debuted in theaters on Aug. 21.
Ullom mostly rejects the comparisons to other recent breakout Gen Z horror directors like Obsession 's Curry Barker and Backrooms ' Kane Parsons.

articles.title: Nintendo’s Forgotten ‘90s Mario Spinoff Deserves a Switch 2 Reboot
articles.summary: Over the years, Nintendo has made tons of fantastic spinoffs based on its iconic red-capped plumber. From Mario Kart and Mario Party to Luigi’s Mansion and Wario Ware, the charming world of the Mushroom Kingdom transcends genre boundaries.
body: Released in 1992 for the Super Nintendo, Mario Paint sold just shy of 2.5 million copies worldwide. That ranks among the platform’s top 20 best-selling games, just above Super Mario RPG and a few notches below Chrono Trigger. It wasn’t really a game in the traditional sense, but an approachable digital art studio that also featured a music composer, a pixel-art editor, and tools to make simple animations. Mario Paint was bundled with the SNES Mouse and a simple plastic mousepad, which were required to play it.

Despite its popularity, Mario Paint never got a direct sequel… outside Japan, anyway. The closest Nintendo may have come was when it launched Mario no Photopi for the N64 in 1998. The Japan-only game allowed players to upload their own digital camera photos and alter them with cute frames and stamps, like those Print Club photobooth stickers. The company also sold optional clip art packs featuring Hello Kitty, Bomberman, Yoshi, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. If learning about this for the first time makes you jealous, I’m right there with you.
points: Over the years, Nintendo has made tons of fantastic spinoffs based on its iconic red-capped plumber.

articles.title: Ray Chase, the voice of Cyclops in X-Men '97, has '1,000 freaking hours' in Slay the Spire and is running a 'smell build' in Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2: ' I wear perfumes and walk into battle with my fancy boy outfit'
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: Welcome to Disk Cleanup, our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"

Ray Chase's first encounter with PC gaming was on an old DOS computer from his father's accounting job. He grew up on a digital diet of shareware demos from PC gaming's golden era. "My grandfather gave me this basket of shareware games, and we played them nonstop for years," Chase recalls. "There was Duke Nukem 1 and 2. There was Ken's Labyrinth. Blake Stone: Aliens of Gold. There was Wolfenstein 3D, of course. Jack Pack was one of my favourites because it had a level editor."

A voice actor since the early 2000s, Chase has appeared in hundreds of games, films and TV shows. He played the lead character Noctis in Final Fantasy 15, and currently voices Cyclops in X-Men '97, which just aired season two and is in the process of recording season four: "The stuff that's going on in the seasons we're recording now, I guess we'll see in a couple of years, but it's really cool, man."

articles.title: Sony sends PlayStation users a reminder they don't own their digital games just as a fan boycott over ending discs kicks off
articles.summary: PlayStation users have received an unprompted reminder of exactly what they do and don't own on the platform, days before a planned boycott over Sony's decision to end new PlayStation discs from 2028.
body: "For your convenience and future reference, we have included full copies of the Terms in this email. Please retain this email for your records."

Several recipients said they'd received the email despite not touching their PS4 or PS5 in months. Rather than linking out to the full terms, the email reproduced each referenced document in full, including the section of the Software EULA covering digital purchases.

"The Software is licensed to you, not sold," it reads. "You are granted a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, and personal license to play or use the Software for your private, non-commercial use on the system or device it was intended for." The terms go on to restrict things like renting, modifying, or obtaining games through unauthorised means.

The email comes just as an attempted PlayStation boycott gets underway. Organised by fan group DoesItPlay, the #PSBlackout campaign runs from 23rd to 30th August and asks participants to log off, avoid purchases, and cancel subscriptions in protest at Sony's move away from physical media.
points: PlayStation users have received an unprompted reminder of exactly what they do and don't own on the platform, days before a planned boycott over Sony's decision to end new PlayStation discs from 2028.

articles.title: If you're desperate for more Baldur's Gate 3, here's a 6-hour mini-campaign all about Astarion with 4 different endings and 6 new companions
articles.summary: We don't really need more Baldur's Gate 3, given how vast and replayable Larian Studios' RPG already is. That said, I'd never say no to more adventures within Larian's highly flexible adaptation of the Forgotten Realms.
body: A Dream of Silence ReVamped (via GamesRadar ) is a mini-campaign based on a text game of the same name created by developer Abigail Corfman. The mod is divided into three acts which have been released separately over the last twelve months. With the release of the third and final act, however, the mod has been packaged and released as a single story.

The story itself takes place in Astarion's mind. But before you dismiss this as a hackneyed 'it was all a dream' narrative—the dreamscape of this particular tale is under the control of a Bastellus—essentially living nightmares that feed on dream energy. To help Astarion escape the Bastellus' grasp, your character—who is projected into Astarion's mind—must accompany him through an even more twisted version of Cazador's dungeon.
points: We don't really need more Baldur's Gate 3, given how vast and replayable Larian Studios' RPG already is.
That said, I'd never say no to more adventures within Larian's highly flexible adaptation of the Forgotten Realms.

articles.title: Gunstoppable gives me the same head-empty unbridled joy as Ultrakill—it doesn't hurt that Gabriel's voice actor is in it too
articles.summary: I like thinking as much as the next guy. It can be really fun to play a videogame that challenges your mental prowess, as it encourages you to weigh up every strategic shred of dialogue or split-second decision.
body: Usually, when I want to scratch this itch I play something like Ultrakill, but now I can add another game to the rotation: Gunstoppable. And let me tell you, it lives up to the name.

It's an action roguelike in which you grapple, slide, and wall run around various maps killing whatever poor robot falls into your path. You're ultimately doing this to save your family and take down the evil billionaire ruling class, one of which is the CEO who made you into the killing machine you are today.

Ok, so the story isn't going to win any Pulitzers, but that's fine because the action is where it's at. You can dual wield weapons, whether that be automatic rifles, knives, or rocket launchers, and as you progress through the levels you also get the chance to upgrade said weapons from a pool of randomly selected bonuses.

Some are pretty basic, like Adrenaline Shot which grants you double attack speed after taking damage, or Rocket Recoil which upgrades any attack so it launches you back when you fire a gun (and also adds force per stack). But there are other more niche upgrades like building into your grapple hook with Supply Hook, which restores ammo.
points: It can be really fun to play a videogame that challenges your mental prowess, as it encourages you to weigh up every strategic shred of dialogue or split-second decision.

articles.title: What's your video game happy place?
articles.summary: We all have our happy places: somewhere - real or otherwise - to escape, relax, and replenish away from the stresses of the modern world. Perhaps yours is in nature, lost in the reverie of a spirited hike up a windy hill, or sweatily squatting your cares away amid the pounding Daruda Sandstorms of…
body: As you might have noticed, it's Optimism Week here on Eurogamer - a chance, at a time it isn't always easy to remember, to reflect on how special video games can be. And to celebrate the occasion, we're reviving The Big Question to tackle another topical talking point before wafting it lovingly over to you. And this time: what's your video game happy place?

Do you prefer to take solace in the cosy idylls of the farming life, sinking dreamily into the comforting mundanity of turnip whispering? Perhaps your gaming happy place is one of nostalgia, the warmth of a retro favourite of old. As it happens, I've already written about one of my own favourite happy places: the vast procedural universe of No Man's Sky, where I can amble serenely with the vaguest of purposes, tweak my infinitely expanding base, dip into its wonderfully kind community, or idly tinker with its latest toys. But I've got other happy places, far removed: harsher, crueller worlds to explore.

articles.title: Arc Raiders' fifth Expedition will be its last until early 2027
articles.summary: Embark Studios has confirmed that Arc Raiders ' fifth Expedition, opening next month, will be the last one players see until early 2027.
body: "We have been carefully reviewing your feedback on Expeditions, and while we've made ongoing improvements along the way, we've come to realise that some of the issues you've raised, like the tight departure windows, the reward structure, and accessibility for new players, need more than incremental fixes," Embark said in a blog post. "They call for bigger changes."

The update added: "In order to address those concerns, we need to pause the Expeditions for a while. The fifth Expedition will be the last one until early 2027, when Expeditions will return with major improvements, tackling some of the biggest player pain points. So, if you've been on the fence about departing - now is the time! We will share more details on what those changes will look like in September."

The Expedition Window opens on 8th September and closes on 29th September, giving three weeks rather than the previous two. Quest progress reset, previously mandatory, is now opt-in for players who'd rather keep their quest line going than start over, though the Hullcracker Blueprint (normally tied to that quest line) will need an alternative route to unlock as a result.
points: Embark Studios has confirmed that Arc Raiders ' fifth Expedition, opening next month, will be the last one players see until early 2027.

articles.title: This newly announced soulslike has a main character inspired by Dark Souls' most heartbreaking boss fight
articles.summary: Honestly, I'm surprised nobody thought of this sooner. Via Kotaku, Stray Dog: Nobody Cares is a soulslike directly inspired by Dark Souls, which asks: "What if you played as Great Grey Wolf Sif?" It's an idea that seems painfully obvious in hindsight, and I can only credit developer Parry Frames…
body: Obviously, you don't actually play as Sif in Stray Dog: Nobody Cares. But Knight Artorius' lupine companion is clearly the archetype behind Parry Frames' four-legged protagonist. Even the backstory is similar, with you playing the faithful friend of a knight-errant in a dark fantasy kingdom. When its master is captured, the hound takes it upon itself to track him down and release him.

In its basic structure, Stray Dog appears to be a straightforward dark-fantasy soulslike—offering a world of crumbling ruins, undead enemies, bonfires and boss fights. Much like Sif, your hound fights with a sword in its mouth, and its acrobatic combat style strongly recalls Sif's own balletic sweeps and pirouettes.

Developer Parry Frames says there will be "multiple" combat styles that players can learn, and they'll be able to parry, backstab, and perform deathblows on enemies in the classic Dark Souls style. Stealth will play a role too, though Parry Frames doesn't provide much detail on this front.
points: Honestly, I'm surprised nobody thought of this sooner.

articles.title: GTA 6 Leaker Releases More Gameplay Videos Despite Rockstar Owner Take-Two's Microsoft and Discord Subpoenas
articles.summary: The alleged GTA 6 leaker has released two further gameplay videos despite Rockstar owner Take-Two's subpoenas requesting identifying information from Microsoft and Discord.
body: The ‘CyberLeek’ person or group released two new videos today, August 22, one showing more supercar gameplay and an armed robbery, the other strip club gameplay. The latter appears to taunt Take-Two and Rockstar by showing a snippet of a cutscene in which a character says they need to take "a leak." This is the second cutscene to emerge this week, and there is growing concern that the leaker has access to a build of the game and may post significant story spoilers.
These new videos are the seventh and eighth to leak this week. And, like all the others, they advertise the ‘CyberLeek’ memecoin as part of what is widely considered to be a crypto scheme.

On August 20, Take-Two issued Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) subpoenas in a federal court requesting information from both Microsoft and Discord as part of its hunt for the leaker or leakers behind the recent spate of GTA 6 gameplay videos. Take-Two wants identifying information associated with user accounts that were members of a number of Discord servers, including one relating to Australian GTA content creator Matthew "Matt" Judge, aka DarkViperAU. Judge has denied any wrongdoing.
points: The alleged GTA 6 leaker has released two further gameplay videos despite Rockstar owner Take-Two's subpoenas requesting identifying information from Microsoft and Discord.

videos.title: The Biggest Game Releases of September 2026
videos.summary: This September has become one of the most jam-packed release windows on record, bringing a non-stop wave of massive blockbusters and cozy indie hits. From Insomniac’s long-awaited take on Wolverine, to nostalgic arcade slashers, and psychological horror, this month has something for every type of…
body: This month’s Biggest Game Releases video highlights major upcoming games including Marvel's Wolverine, The Blood of Dawnwalker, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Halloween: The Game, Control Resonant, Silent Hill Townfall, Fire Emblem Fortune’s Weave, Dune Awakening, and EA Sports FC 27. We also cover a multitude of indie deckbuilders, cozy management titles, and everything in between. In this video you can also expect Max to touch on games such as Garfield Escape From Monday, Minecraft Dungeons 2, RuneScape Dragonwilds, Hot Wheels Infinite Rush and many more across PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 1, Switch 2, and PC.
points: This September has become one of the most jam-packed release windows on record, bringing a non-stop wave of massive blockbusters and cozy indie hits.
Join IGN’s Max Scoville as he breaks down the biggest titles dropping across all of your favorite gaming platforms in September 2026.
